editions.title: October 26, 2026
editions.dek: Day of the Dead fills the Mission, nine Warriors home dates land at Chase Center, and Dickens Fair Early Bird pricing ends October 31.

editions.title: October 21, 2026
editions.dek: Jose Mourinho takes Real Madrid back to the Camp Nou on Sunday six points adrift of an unbeaten Barcelona and without Vinicius Junior.

editions.title: October 20, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal go to the Allianz Arena as English champions with a perfect Champions League record and a scoring problem nobody has solved yet.

editions.title: October 14, 2026
editions.dek: Paris Saint-Germain, winners of the last two Champions Leagues, visit an unbeaten Manchester City on a matchday that has already produced 32 goals in nine games.

editions.title: October 13, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal followed Mikel Arteta's new contract to 2030 with a comeback win over Leeds and a 3-0 Champions League rout of Lille, in a week that ended with the death of Ken Friar.

editions.title: October 12, 2026
editions.dek: The Valkyries host the first WNBA Finals games ever played in San Francisco, the Warriors open at home, and autumn festivals run from Half Moon Bay to Sonoma.

editions.title: October 7, 2026
editions.dek: Manchester City lodged their appeal against the guilty verdict at 7pm on 1 October, starting a twelve-week clock that will decide when, and how hard, any punishment lands.

editions.title: October 6, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal return from a three week international break second in the table with eight goals in five games and the sharpest question of their season still unanswered.

editions.title: September 30, 2026
editions.dek: An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of serious financial breaches across nine seasons, and the sanction is still to come.

editions.title: September 29, 2026
editions.dek: With no Arsenal men's match all week, Mikel Arteta agreed a reported four-year deal and Manchester City were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

editions.title: September 28, 2026
editions.dek: A catch-up edition for five weeks of fall: Fleet Week, Hardly Strictly, Valkyries playoff nights, pumpkins on the coast and a Halloween weekend.

editions.title: September 23, 2026
editions.dek: UEFA and FIFA are at war over who owns the World Cup, and this week the fight moved openly into the 2027 election campaign.

editions.title: September 22, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal and Mikel Arteta have agreed a new long-term contract, the BBC reports, three days after Brighton beat the champions 3-0 on the south coast.

editions.title: September 16, 2026
editions.dek: Europe's great managerial reshuffle faces its first verdicts as Maresca's Manchester City go four from four and Mourinho's Real Madrid chase Barcelona.

editions.title: September 15, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal begin the Carabao Cup at Ipswich six months after losing its final, unbeaten in six and missing half a back four.

editions.title: September 14, 2026
editions.dek: A catch-up edition for mid-September to mid-October: Portola, Folsom, Hardly Strictly, Fleet Week, the Giants' last homestand and the Valkyries' run-in.

editions.title: September 9, 2026
editions.dek: The Champions League league phase opens on a redrawn map of Europe, with Mourinho at Real Madrid, Maresca at City and the holders PSG 14th in France.

editions.title: September 8, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal open their Champions League campaign at Napoli on Wednesday with William Saliba out, Ezri Konsa two games into his Arsenal career and Martin Odegaard in the form of his life.

editions.title: September 2, 2026
editions.dek: A record 3.46 billion pound Premier League window closed with Enzo Fernandez joining Manchester City for 125m and two agreed deals collapsing after the buzzer.

editions.title: September 1, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal close the window having sold Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Malick Fofana and loaned Ethan Nwaneri to Dortmund, all while unbeaten and yet to concede.

editions.title: August 31, 2026
editions.dek: Labor Day weekend opens a five-week run that ends with Hardly Strictly free in the park, plus Portola, Folsom and the Giants' last homestand.

editions.title: August 26, 2026
editions.dek: Six days from the September 1 deadline, a World Cup summer has pushed Europe's most expensive week into the middle of the season.

editions.title: August 25, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal open the title defence with two 3-0 wins and six days left to remake a forward line, with Gabriel Martinelli close to a record Saudi exit.

editions.title: August 19, 2026
editions.dek: Europe restarts 33 days after the World Cup with ten new Premier League managers, Rodri sold to Barcelona and Pep Guardiola gone after a decade.

editions.title: August 18, 2026
editions.dek: Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence against Coventry on Friday, three days after a 3-0 Community Shield win and with the centre-back department still unfixed.

editions.title: August 17, 2026
editions.dek: Outside Lands packed up ten days ago and Stern Grove closed with Al Green yesterday afternoon.
